rationale: Stem ('most directly reflects which Progressive Era idea?') asks the student to identify which historical concept the boarding-club proposal exemplifies -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Topic constrained to U6: 6.11 Reform in the Gilded Age is the closest reform fit. NOTE: item's period field appears mislabeled — Hull House strike account by Jane Addams (1910) is Period 7 content (belongs under 7.4 The Progressives), not U6.

Stem ('Logan's speech best illustrates which of the following?') asks the student to identify and describe the claim/main idea in the text source (cycles of revenge and retaliatory violence on the frontier) -> 3.A (Identify and describe a claim and/or argument in a text-based or non-text-based source). Logan's 1774 speech falls in the Revolutionary era: 3.5 The American Revolution.

Stem asks whose rhetorical approach Carter's 1980 approach most closely resembled -> identifying a pattern/connection among historical developments (Carter 1980 vs Truman 1948) -> 5.A (Identify patterns among or connections between historical developments and processes). Carter-era 1980 content -> 8.14 Society in Transition.

Stem ('Prescott's portrayal of Cortes most clearly reflects...') asks the student to identify the source's point of view/historical situation (19th-century romantic 'great man' historiography) -> 2.A (Identify a source's point of view, purpose, historical situation, and/or audience). Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire -> 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest.

Stem asks what funding mechanism the 'Share Our Wealth' plan relied on -> identifying the evidence/mechanism used in the source to support Long's argument -> 3.B (Identify the evidence used in a source to support an argument). 1934 Long proposal as Depression-era alternative/critique of FDR -> 7.10 The New Deal.

Stem ('Bush's new world order rhetoric was prompted most directly by...') asks the student to identify the historical context (Iraq's invasion of Kuwait) behind a specific development -> 4.A (Identify and describe a historical context for a specific historical development or process). 1990 post-Cold War collective-security rhetoric -> 9.3 The End of the Cold War.

Stem asks which European power destroyed the French Florida settlement -> identifying a historical development (Spanish destruction of Fort Caroline, 1565) -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Early European colonization rivalry -> 2.2 European Colonization.

Stem ('contributed most directly to which of the following?') asks the student to identify the development that followed from the depicted conditions (white-supremacist terror hardening into segregation/Plessy) -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). 1874 Nast cartoon of White League/KKK terror -> 5.11 Failure of Reconstruction.

Stem ('The migration Parkman described intensified sectional conflict because...') asks the student to identify the development caused (Congress forced to decide slavery's status in the West) -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). No dedicated westward-migration topic exists in U4; 4.3 Politics and Regional Interests is the closest fit for Oregon Trail-era sectional politics. Low confidence on topic.

Stem ('The Cooper Union Address helped Lincoln by...') asks the student to identify the claim/significance in the source (national debut introducing him to eastern Republicans before the 1860 nomination) -> 3.A (Identify and describe a claim and/or argument in a text-based or non-text-based source). Lincoln's 1860 nomination -> 5.7 Election of 1860 and Secession. Low confidence on skill: the item tests the source's historical significance more than argument structure.

Stem asks what Penn's 1701 Charter of Privileges was a forerunner of -> identifying a connection between historical developments across time (colonial charter -> First Amendment) -> 5.A (Identify patterns among or connections between historical developments and processes). Pennsylvania colony governance -> 2.3 The Regions of British Colonies.

Stem asks for the first important cash crop in the American colonies (tobacco) -> identifying a historical development/process -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Chesapeake tobacco economy -> 2.3 The Regions of British Colonies.

EXCEPT question on why colonists objected to post-1763 Parliamentary policies -> identifying historical concepts/developments (colonists' grievances, salutary neglect, representation) -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Direct match: 3.3 Taxation Without Representation.

Stem asks how Marshall strengthened the Court (judicial review, Marbury v. Madison) -> identifying a historical development/process -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Marshall Court in the early republic -> 4.2 The Rise of Political Parties and the Era of Jefferson.

EXCEPT question testing facts about the temperance movement -> identifying historical concepts/developments -> 1.A (Identify a historical concept, development, or process). Temperance as a 19th-century reform movement -> 4.11 An Age of Reform.
